title: How he learned cornet
summary: He was largely self-taught, took from a relative Oscar Giovanni, learned to read and study harmony after leaving New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I wonder, did he ever talk about who his teacher was, or if he had more than one teacher? Well, no.
Or he went to school, or anything to learn with Carnet?
Well, no. He took it up with a relation of him by the name of Oscar Giovanni. Oscar Giovanni. Mm-hmm. But he never had no regular teacher. He just picked it up himself.
Most of them picked it up himself.

Because, uh, his grandmother, this old lady, said that he, uh, even when he was playing as a child, he'd get clothespins and make a carnet, you know? Oh, I like that. And he'd play on top the other day, and he'd just play that, put two on the top and try to... That guy is a carnet. ...bella carnet, you know, and he'd play from a child. And you did tell me that he took a few lessons with, uh... Shalini. Shalini. You know, off and on, people that knew more than him, you know, he would go around then. But I don't know of him having any teaching. And then he would go with, uh, with old men, could be his father at the time. And, you know, and play, stand around and play with them. And, well then at that time he was playing without no music, you see? Yes. He was playing by ear. It's when he left here, that's where he began to play, you know, and read it. Right, music very well. And study harmony and everything. And he'd sit down there with a book all night. He had to have a teacher because he knew music too well.
Oh yes, he must have studied music.

Because he could take a 16, a 64, a 32, And he had a second note from the eights. He knew all of that. Yeah. And he studied all that, you see. But he, Mama says it was after he went away. He played very well, even before he studied that, he must have played very well. Yeah.
And we know that the Levita had stack of music. Well he could read music. Oh yeah. Everybody knows that. Oh yeah. Yes.

He used to have that on the space shelf. Well I knew the music. Because you see, he could read music, you know. But he would take, to hold his music on that little horn there, a clothespin. I said, what, you gonna wash tonight? He said, no. He said, no, I wanna hold up the fans going my music on. Oh yeah, yeah.
